TVK1.claim: Vikarabad is about 70 km from Hyderabad in the Anantagiri Hills, whose highlight is the Anantha Padmanabha Swamy temple to Vishnu.

evidence.quote: xplore Vikarabad Vikarabad is a charming, scenic town located about 70 kilometers from Hyderabad, nestled in the picturesque hills of the Anantagiri Hills in the state of Telangana.

This temple on Ananthagiri hills is dedicated to worship Lord Vishnu. According to Hindu Mythology, Skanda Purana, it is believed that this Sri Anantha Padmanabha Swamy temple was constructed by the rishi Markandeya in the dwapara yuga on Ananthagiri hills.

TVK2.claim: Activities include moderate treks in the Anantagiri Hills, including to the Bhoolokeshwar Temple, kayaking at Kotpally Reservoir (about 60 km from Hyderabad), camping and birdwatching.

evidence.quote: Trekking in Anantagiri Hills Difficulty Level : Moderate
You can also trek to the Bhoolokeshwar Temple , perched atop the hills, while enjoying the tranquility and fresh air of the forest.
Situated about 60 kilometers from Hyderabad, Kotpally Reservoir is a serene spot, perfect for those looking to enjoy a day out surrounded by nature while engaging in some adventure.
The area is a haven for birdwatching, where you can spot a variety of species, including migratory birds during the right season.

TVK3.claim: Local food is Telangana-style: spicy vegetarian curries, Hyderabadi-style biryani and snacks such as mirchi bajji.

evidence.quote: Spicy vegetarian curries and rice-based dishes like Biryani (in the Hyderabadi style) are common. If you're in the mood for street food, look for local snacks like Mirchi Bajji (fried green chilies) and Chili Chicken .

TVK4.claim: The Skanda Purana says the sage Markandeya built the temple; the forests suit eco-tourism, with camping, bonfires and migratory birds in season, and the town makes a weekend or day trip from Hyderabad.

evidence.quote: it is believed that this Sri Anantha Padmanabha Swamy temple was constructed by the rishi Markandeya
make it a great spot for eco-tourism
where you can set up tents, enjoy a bonfire under the stars

TBH1.claim: Bhadrachalam is a pilgrimage town on the Godavari, home to the Sri Seetha Ramachandra Swamy Devasthanam, a temple to Rama that draws devotees in lakhs.

evidence.quote: The temple town of Bhadrachalam is situated on the banks of Godavari River. The town shares its historical significance with Ramayana Era.
Sri Seetha Ramachandra Swamy Devasthanam A sacred place that attracts lakhs of devotees from all over the world, it is the abode of Lord Rama (The seventh incarnation of Sri Mahavishnu).

TBH2.claim: Tradition places Rama, Sita and Lakshmana's forest exile here, and Parnashala, linked to the golden deer and Sita's abduction, is nearby.

evidence.quote: This coherent hill place existed in “Dandakaranya” of Ramayana period where Rama with his consort Sita and brother Laxmana had spent their vanavasa and Parnashaala (the place connected to the famous Golden Deer and the place from where Sita was abducted by Ravana.) is also in the vicinity of this temple site.
is also in the vicinity of this temple site.

TBH3.claim: Kinnerasani Wildlife Sanctuary, 12 km from Palvancha, covers 635.4 sq km with leopards, spotted deer and gaur.

evidence.quote: Kinnerasani Wildlife Sanctuary The Kinnerasani Wildlife Sanctuary is located at a distance of 12 kilometers away from Palvancha town. The wildlife sanctuary covers an area of 635.4 square kilometers and is home to a rich wildlife, including leopards, spotted deer and gaurs, besides different bird species.

TYG1.claim: Yadagirigutta, visited by thousands of pilgrims daily, is the hill shrine of Lakshmi Narasimha, worshipped here in five forms as a Pancharama Narasimha Kshetra.

evidence.quote: The place is visited by thousands of pilgrims every day. According to the Hindu scriptures or Puranas of the Third Age, there was a sage named Yadarshi, who was the son of the great sage Sri Rishyasringa Maharshi and Santa Devi.

The Swami himself manifested himself in five different forms as Sri Jwala Narasimha, Sri Gandabherunda, Sri Yogananda, Sri Ugra and Sri Lakshminarasimha after Swami and is therefore worshiped as the Pancharama Narasimha Kshetra.

TYG2.claim: Legend says Narasimha appeared to the sage Yadarshi, son of Rishyasringa, who meditated in a cave here.

evidence.quote: According to the Hindu scriptures or Puranas of the Third Age, there was a sage named Yadarshi, who was the son of the great sage Sri Rishyasringa Maharshi and Santa Devi.

Sri Narasimha Swami appeared before him, pleased with his devotion. The Swami himself manifested himself in five different forms as Sri Jwala Narasimha, Sri Gandabherunda, Sri Yogananda, Sri Ugra and Sri Lakshminarasimha after Swami and is therefore worshiped as the Pancharama Narasimha Kshetra.

TYG3.claim: Near Yadagirigutta is Surendrapuri, a temple-art complex with scenes from the epics and replicas of major temples; it takes about two hours.

evidence.quote: Surendrapuri The Surendrapuri Hanumadeswarar Temple located near Yadagirigutta is a must visit place. Kunda Satyanarayana Kaladhamaya is a Hindu temple art exhibition temple.
It takes around two hours to explore the place.

TYG4.claim: Narasimha is said to have appeared in five forms, Jwala, Gandabherunda, Yogananda, Ugra and Lakshminarasimha; the place enjoys a pleasant climate in all seasons; Surendrapuri has scenes from the Mahabharata and Bhagavatam and a huge Shiva statue.

evidence.quote: manifested himself in five different forms as Sri Jwala Narasimha, Sri Gandabherunda, Sri Yogananda, Sri Ugra and Sri Lakshminarasimha
enjoys a harmonious climate in all seasons
The scenes in the epics of Mahabharata and Bhagavatam are impressive. The temple has a huge statue of Lord Shiva.

TBF1.claim: Bhongir (Bhuvanagiri) Fort stands on a monolithic rock about 47 km from Hyderabad; tradition credits its founding to the Western Chalukya king Tribhuvanamalla Vikramaditya VI, after whom it was called Tribhuvanagiri.

evidence.quote: Bhuvanagiri Fort Bhuvanagiri Fort is an ancient monument built on a monolithic rock fortress, about 47 km from the city of Hyderabad. The hill is 610 meters high and is the tallest mountain in Telangana.
It is believed that the western Chalukya ruler Tribuvanamalla Vikramadithya – VI got the fort at this place constructed which was named after him as Tribhuvanagiri.

TBF2.claim: The fort is associated with Rudramadevi and Prataparudra; its gateway resembles Golconda's Fateh Darwaza, and inside are granaries, military quarters and a Shiva temple.

evidence.quote: The fort is associated with the rule of the Kakatiya queen Rudramadevi and her Grandson Prataparudhra. Yadagirigutta Yadagirigutta is a unique and pleasant place that enjoys a harmonious climate in all seasons.
The entrance resembles that of Fateh Darwaza, the first gate of Balahisar in Golconda Fort. Tall walls and spacious rooms are visible in the architecture of Islamic culture.

The inner courtyards of the fort include horseshoes, granaries and military houses. There is a Shiva temple on the hill of Bhuvanagiri, a statue of the black Nandi, Someshwara, Bammadevara temple and a monastery under the hill.
There is a Shiva temple on the hill of Bhuvanagiri, a statue of the black Nandi, Someshwara, Bammadevara temple and a monastery under the hill.

TBF3.claim: From the south the rock looks like a tortoise and from the west like a sleeping elephant; the fort was long ruled by the Qutb Shahis, and a black Nandi statue stands on the hill.

evidence.quote: from the south it looks like a tortoise and a sleeping elephant from the west
Bhuvanagiri Fort was a long time ruled by Qutub Shahi. Historians claim that the coins of the Vishnu Kundi period were found here.
a statue of the black Nandi

TNS1.claim: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam, 124 m high, holds back the Krishna in Nalgonda district and irrigates the lands that earn the region the name 'Rice Bowl of India'.

evidence.quote: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam Telangana owes its famous title ‘Rice Bowl of India’ to Nagarjuna Sagar Dam, which plays a lead role in making the lands of the state fertile.
The 124-meter-high dam
storing massive amount of the waters of Krishna River

TNS2.claim: Nandikonda, beside the dam, was part of the Ikshvaku kingdom; Buddhist pillared halls and monasteries were unearthed there and the relics are shown in the museum.

evidence.quote: Nandikonda Nandikonda is a small village located along the banks of Krishna River in Nalgonda district. It is located close to the magnificent Nagarjuna Sagar dam.
Nandikonda was part of the Ikshvaku Dynasty and the village shot into prominence after scores of ancient Buddhist structures like pillared halls and monasteries were unearthed.
The relics that were unearthed during a series of excavations are today displayed at the Museum here. Rachakonda Fort Telangana region is the home of the incredible Rachakonda Fort.

TNS4.claim: Built between 1955 and 1967, the dam is 1.6 km long with 26 flood gates and straddles the Telangana–Andhra Pradesh border; Nehru inaugurated construction on 10 December 1955, and the project is jointly operated by both states.

evidence.quote: Constructed between 1955 and 1967, the dam created a water reservoir with gross storage capacity of 11.472 billion cubic metres (405.1×10^9 cu ft), its effective capacity is 6.92 cubic km or 244.41 Tmcft.
1.6 kilometres (5,200 ft) long with 26 flood gates
The project's construction was officially inaugurated by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru on 10 December 1955 and proceeded for the next twelve years.

It is jointly operated by Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Nagarjuna Sagar Dam was the first in a series of major infrastructure projects termed as "modern temples" initiated for achieving the Green Revolution in India.

TNS3.claim: Scores of ancient Buddhist structures, such as pillared halls and monasteries, were unearthed at Nandikonda.

evidence.quote: Nandikonda was part of the Ikshvaku Dynasty and the village shot into prominence after scores of ancient Buddhist structures like pillared halls and monasteries were unearthed.

TMD1.claim: Medak, once called Methukudurgam, passed from the Kakatiyas and Bahmanis to the Golconda kings, the Mughals and the Nizams.

evidence.quote: Medak was originally known as Methukudurgam which subsequently changed into Methuku due to the growth of fine and coarse rice in this area.
Medak district was part of the Kakatiya Kingdom as well as Bahmani Kingdom and later the Golconda Nawabs. Finally, with the fall of the Qutub shahi dynasty, it was annexed to the Mughal Empire.
due to the growth of fine and coarse rice in this area
Several coins of the Satavahana rulers

evidence.quote: Hill Fort (Built by Rajas of Warangal) The fort at Medak was originally constructed by the Kakatiya rulers and later developed by the Qutb Shahi rulers. The fort which stands about 90 meters above the surrounding plains is one of the important hill forts in the Deccan region.
The fort which stands about 90 meters above the surrounding plains is one of the important hill forts in the Deccan region.
Inside the fort, a Dutch-made 10 feet long brass gun was placed. Old Mosque Komtoor village is located at a distance of 10 km from Medak Town.

TMD3.claim: Other sights include the Qutb Shahi mosque at Komtoor (10 km), the Kuchadri Venkateswara temple, Medak Cathedral, Pocharam Wildlife Sanctuary and Edupayala temple.

Medak Cathedral Church

TFP1.claim: Falaknuma Palace stands on a hillock about 5 km from Charminar; built for the Paigah family and later the Nizam's, its name means 'like the sky' or 'mirror of the sky'.

evidence.quote: merely 5 kilometres from Hyderabad's iconic Charminar

It was once the pride of the Paigah family and later cherished by the Nizam of Hyderabad. The palace name "Falaknuma" means "like the sky" or "mirror of the sky" in Urdu - a true embodiment of its celestial title.
The palace name "Falaknuma" means "like the sky" or "mirror of the sky" in Urdu - a true embodiment of its celestial title.

TFP2.claim: Designed by the English architect William Ward Marret in Italian marble, it is shaped like a scorpion and holds a 2-ton manually operated organ in the ballroom.

evidence.quote: The English architect William Ward Marret conceived the palace, a marvel sculpted entirely from Italian marble. It is adorned with captivating stained-glass windows that bestow a magical aura upon its majestic exterior.
The palace resembles the shape of a scorpion, with two wing-like structures extending from the north.
The palace also houses hidden treasures, such as a unique, manually operated organ that weighs 2 tons and graces the Ballroom.

TFP3.claim: Private to the Nizam's family for nearly a century, it was restored over nearly a decade from 2000 by about 1,000 artisans and is now a heritage hotel.

evidence.quote: For nearly a century, Falaknuma Palace remained a private sanctuary of the Nizam family, shielded from the public eye until the dawn of the millennium.
With the dedication of nearly 1,000 skilled artisans labouring tirelessly for nearly a decade, the palace was lovingly restored to its former magnificence.
Today, Falaknuma Palace is a magnificent heritage hotel covering an impressive 93,970 square meters.

TFP4.claim: Inside are frescoed and gilded ceilings in the State Reception Room, stained-glass windows, a library of English, Urdu and Persian books, Venetian chandeliers and a billiards room.

evidence.quote: It is adorned with captivating stained-glass windows
where frescoes and gilded reliefs grace the ceiling
a vast collection of books in English, Urdu, and Persian
including famed Venetian chandeliers and the magnificent billiards room

TCM1.claim: Chowmahalla Palace near Charminar was the seat of the Asaf Jahi dynasty and the Nizams' official residence; it is now a museum still owned by the family.

evidence.quote: Chowmahalla Palace, a splendid architectural masterpiece that was once the seat of the Nizams of Hyderabad
It was the seat of power of the Asaf Jahi dynasty (1720–1948) and was the official residence of the Nizams during their reign.

The palace has been converted into a museum and the ownership still lies with the family. The palace was constructed at the location of an earlier palace of the Qutb Shahi dynasty and Asaf Jahi dynasty close to the Charminar.

TCM2.claim: Its name means 'four palaces'; the southern courtyard has four neoclassical palaces around a pond, and the Khilwat Mubarak durbar hall has a marble platform for the royal seat and 19 Belgian-crystal chandeliers.

evidence.quote: The word chār or chahār, and its variation chow, means "four" and the word mahal means "palace" in Urdu, Hindi and Persian.

== Southern courtyard == This is the oldest part of the palace, consisting of four palaces: Afzal Mahal, Mahtab Mahal, Tahniyat Mahal and Aftab Mahal, built symmetrically opposite each other in Neoclassical style.
The grand pillared Durbar Hall has a pure marble platform on which the Takht-e-Nishan or the royal seat was laid.
The 19 chandeliers of Belgian crystal were recently reinstalled to recreate the lost splendour of this regal hall.

TCM3.claim: The family opened the restored palace to the public in January 2005; it shows the Nizams' vintage cars, including a Rolls-Royce, and once covered 45 acres, of which 12 remain.

evidence.quote: The former Nizam (Barkat Ali Khan Mukarram Jah) and his family decided to restore the Chowmahalla Palace and open it to the public in January 2005.
The palace also has a collection of vintage cars, including the Rolls-Royce, which the Nizam kings used.
The palace originally covered 45 acres (180,000 m2), but only 12 acres (49,000 m2) remain today.

TCM4.claim: Construction began in the late 18th century; the southern palaces have Ionic and Corinthian columns, while the northern courtyard has Mughal domes and Persian stucco work.

evidence.quote: Construction began in the late 18th century and over the decades a synthesis of many architectural styles and influences emerged.

The columns in the Aftab Mahal and Mehtab Mahal are of Ionic order whereas the Afzal Mahal and Tehniyat Mahal have Corinthian columns. == Northern courtyard == This part has Bara Imam, a long corridor of rooms on the east side facing the central fountain and pool that once housed the administrative wing; and Shishe-Alat, meaning mirror image.
It has Mughal domes and arches and many Persian elements such as the ornate stucco works that adorn the Khilwat Mubarak.

TQT1.claim: The Qutb Shahi Tombs, 1 km north of Golconda Fort's Banjara Darwaza, are where the kings of Golconda are buried together, in the Ibrahim Bagh gardens.

evidence.quote: They are located one kilometer north of Golconda Fort’s called Banjara Darwaza. They are imposing marvels of architectural excellence that stand as the reminders of the glory of Golconda kings who are buried at the same spot.

They resemble Persian, Pathan and Hindu architectural styles that makes use of grey granite, with stucco ornamentation and is a one-of-its-kind place in the world where the whole dynasty is buried at a single spot.
surrounded by landscape gardens called Ibrahim Bagh

TQT2.claim: The domed tombs of grey granite with stucco rise from square bases, 9 to 15 m above the terrace, the largest 42.5 m high; their domes were once covered in blue and green tiles.

evidence.quote: that makes use of grey granite, with stucco ornamentation
Each tomb is of quadrangular shape and rises around 9 to 15 meters above the terrace. The smaller tombs constitute single stories while the larger tombs are seen as two storied.
magnificent tomb with a height of 42.5 m covered by large dome

The domes actually constituted of blue and green tiles, whereas only few pieces exist now. The Qutub Shahi Tombs are surrounded by enchanting minarets and there is magnificent tomb with a height of 42.5 m covered by large dome.

TQT3.claim: Neglected after the dynasty fell, they were restored under Salar Jung III and are usually visited together with Golconda Fort.

evidence.quote: The tombs were neglected after their reign until Salar Jung III took up their restoration works during the early 19th century.
It is a popular destination in the tourist circuit of Hyderabad and visitors coming to Golconda fort donot miss the tombs, which are marketed as a clubbed destination.

TQT4.claim: Built by the Qutb Shahis, they are among Hyderabad's oldest monuments, in Persian, Pathan and Hindu styles; smaller tombs are single-storeyed and larger ones two-storeyed.

evidence.quote: these tombs are considered to be among the oldest historical monuments of Hyderabad

evidence.quote: The temple houses three idols: one each of Lord Rishabha, Lord Neminath, and Lord Mahaveer. The temple is about 77 km from Hyderabad on the Hyderabad-Warangal Highway.
The temple is about 77 km from Hyderabad on the Hyderabad-Warangal Highway. The Kolanupaka Temple is said to be more than two thousand years old.

evidence.quote: Rajahmundry is one of Andhra Pradesh’s oldest and most culturally vibrant cities. Often regarded as the cultural capital of the region, the city blends literary heritage, riverine landscapes, spiritual landmarks, and a relaxed pace of life.
Often regarded as the cultural capital of the region, the city blends literary heritage, riverine landscapes, spiritual landmarks, and a relaxed pace of life.

ARJ2.claim: Sights include the Godavari rail bridge, the ghats, ISKCON Rajahmundry, the Markandeya temple, Dowleswaram Barrage and boat cruises through the Papi Hills.

evidence.quote: One of the city’s most striking landmarks is the Godavari Rail Bridge , an engineering marvel that stretches across the river and offers stunning views, especially at sunrise and sunset.
A short drive from the city leads to Dowleswaram Barrage , where the Godavari branches into canals that nourish the fertile delta.
Nature lovers can explore Papi Hills , a picturesque stretch of forested hills best experienced via a boat cruise on the Godavari.
The Markandeya Temple , dedicated to Sage Markandeya

It connects Hyderabad, Chennai, and Bangalore. Taxis and cabs are accessible from the airport to the city center.

By Road: The city is well linked via NH216 and state highways. Buses travel often from Hyderabad, Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam , and other cities.

Kumararama Bheemeshwara Swamy Temple, Samalkot - One of the five Pancharama Kshetras

the Sri Sathya Sai Space Theatre (Planetarium) bridges science and spirituality

ALP1.claim: The Lepakshi (Sri Veerabhadra) Temple is a 16th-century Vijayanagara temple, a centrally protected monument famed for its carvings, frescoes and hanging pillar.

evidence.quote: Dedicated to Lord Veerabhadra, a fierce form of Lord Shiva, this 16th-century marvel flourished under the reign of the Vijayanagara kings. Step within and be mesmerised by the intricate carvings and vibrant frescoes that adorn nearly every surface.
a centrally protected monument of national importance
The famed hanging pillar, defying logic for centuries, is a testament to the architectural genius of its creators.

ALP2.claim: The Natya Mandapa ceiling murals show scenes from the epics and Puranas, including a huge mural of Veerabhadra; the Kalyana Mandapa was left unfinished.

evidence.quote: Prepare to be dazzled by the Natya Mandapa (dance pavilion), the most ornate structure within the temple complex. Its ceilings are adorned with breathtaking murals depicting scenes from the Mahabharata, Ramayana, and Puranas.
The central masterpiece is a colossal mural of Lord Veerabhadra, possibly the largest in Asia.
A veil of mystery surrounds the unfinished Kalyana Mandapa, believed to be the celestial wedding venue of Shiva and Parvati.

ALP3.claim: Nearby, a monolithic Nandi 15 feet high and 27 feet long faces the temple's Nagalinga; the temple is open 6 am to 6 pm and the Lepakshi Utsavam is usually around March.

the Nandi faces the Nagalingeshwara sculpture housed within the temple

the annual Lepakshi Utsavam (usually held around March)

Explore the Nagalinga, a powerful Shiva linga sheltered by a seven—hooded snake.

one of the most spectacular Vijayanagara temples
Located atop Kumarasailam, a low—lying hill resembling a tortoise
the temple houses the only surviving fresco paintings from this era

The town is classified as both a Jyotirlinga and a Shakta pitha. As of 2001 census of India, Srisailam had a population of 23,257.

The travel by road is not allowed to Srisailam between 9:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. as roads are through Nallamala forests. Rail The nearest railway station is at Markapur Road Railway Station, about 83.1 kilometres from Srisailam.

an inscription of Bukkaraya mentions this place as ‘King of Forts’
the steep rocky hills that reach a height of more than 680 metres

ACG1.claim: Chandragiri Fort, near Tirupati, covers 25 acres; founded in the 11th century by Yadava rulers, it was fortified by the Vijayanagara Empire in the 15th century.

evidence.quote: It covers an area of 25 acres and is known for its remarkable architecture, historical significance, and stunning surroundings.

Originally established in the 11th century by the Yadava Naidu rulers of the Yaduvada Nadudu state, it was later fortified by the Vijayanagara Empire in the 15th century. Chandragiri Fort is a symbol of both architectural brilliance and strategic acumen exhibited by its creators.

ACG2.claim: The lower fort's three-storeyed Raja Mahal is now a museum of weapons, sculptures and coins, beside the two-storeyed Rani Mahal; Krishnadevaraya stayed here on pilgrimages to Tirumala.

evidence.quote: Raja Mahal stands tall with its three-storeyed grandeur, now home to a mesmerising museum housing an extraordinary collection of weaponry, sculptures, coins, and historical documents.
Nearby, Rani Mahal beckons with its charming two-storeyed layout and a touch of pink from its restoration.

Sri Krishnadevaraya would reside here during his pilgrimages to Tirumala. Additionally, within its major royal rooms is a museum displaying various artifacts dating back to 15th and 16th century stone figures and carvings, offering visitors a fascinating glimpse into Chandragiri's surroundings.

ACG3.claim: Open 10 am to 5 pm; the climb to the upper fort is demanding.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 10:00 AM Closing time - 05:00 PM
Although the climb is demanding, the lure of historical ruins and breathtaking scenery promises an adventure of unparalleled wonder.

ACG4.claim: Chandragiri means 'hill of the moon'; Kapilendra Dev took it in 1460; the lower fort is crescent-shaped and the upper fort has ramparts and watchtowers.

evidence.quote: The name Chandragiri, meaning 'hill of the moon,'

Talakona's waters have healing and spiritual energy

AKG1.claim: Kailasagiri is a hilltop park in Visakhapatnam with sea views, named after Shiva; it was named 'Best Tourist Spot' by the Andhra Pradesh government in 2003.

evidence.quote: Kailasagiri is a place that has earned the title of "Best Tourist Spot" by the Government of Andhra Pradesh in 2003. And it's easy to see why! The lush greenery, the cool breeze, and the panoramic views of the ocean make it a paradise for nature lovers and adventure seekers alike.

places.seoDescription: Vikarabad and the Ananthagiri Hills, about 70 km from Hyderabad: forest treks, the Anantha Padmanabha Swamy temple, kayaking at Kotpally and camping.

overview.text: Vikarabad is a small town about 70 km from Hyderabad, set in the forested Anantagiri Hills and popular as a weekend escape from the city. The hills are cool, green and good for trekking, picnics and photography. On them stands the Sri Anantha Padmanabha Swamy temple, dedicated to Vishnu, which the Skanda Purana says was built by the sage Markandeya. The forests around the town are rich in birds and plant life, and Telangana Tourism promotes the area for eco-tourism: moderate treks to the hill temples, kayaking and boating at Kotpally Reservoir, camping with bonfires near the hills, and easy nature walks for birdwatching, including migratory birds in season. It is a relaxed, rural place that suits a day trip or a quiet weekend.

places.seoDescription: Bhadrachalam on the Godavari: the Sri Seetha Ramachandra Swamy temple, Parnashala of the Ramayana, and Kinnerasani Wildlife Sanctuary nearby.

overview.text: Bhadrachalam is a temple town on the banks of the Godavari in Bhadradri Kothagudem district, which borders Andhra Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. Its Sri Seetha Ramachandra Swamy Devasthanam, dedicated to Rama, draws devotees in lakhs. The name comes from Bhadragiri, the hill of Bhadra, around which the river flows. Tradition holds that this was part of Dandakaranya, the forest where Rama, Sita and Lakshmana spent their exile, and Parnashala, the place associated with the golden deer and Sita's abduction by Ravana, is close to the temple. Nature lovers can add Kinnerasani Wildlife Sanctuary, 12 km from Palvancha, a 635.4 sq km stretch of the Dandakaranya forests with leopards, spotted deer, gaur and many birds.

places.summary: Hilltop Lakshmi Narasimha shrine visited by thousands of pilgrims every day.
places.seoTitle: Yadagirigutta (Yadadri) Temple: Lakshmi Narasimha Shrine, Telangana
places.seoDescription: Yadagirigutta (Yadadri), Telangana: the hilltop Lakshmi Narasimha temple, its legend of the sage Yadarshi, and Surendrapuri nearby.

overview.text: Yadagirigutta, also called Yadadri, is a hilltop Narasimha temple that thousands of pilgrims visit every day. According to the Puranas, the sage Yadarshi, son of Rishyasringa, meditated in a cave here, and Narasimha, pleased with his devotion, appeared before him. The god is said to have manifested in five forms, as Jwala Narasimha, Gandabherunda, Yogananda, Ugra and Lakshminarasimha, which is why the shrine is honoured as a Pancharama Narasimha Kshetra. Telangana Tourism notes that the place enjoys a pleasant climate in every season. Close by is Surendrapuri, a temple-art complex with scenes from the Mahabharata and Bhagavatam, a huge Shiva statue and replicas of major Indian temples; allow about two hours there.

places.seoDescription: Bhongir (Bhuvanagiri) Fort, about 47 km from Hyderabad: a fort on a single monolithic rock linked to the Chalukyas and Kakatiya queen Rudramadevi.

overview.text: Bhongir Fort, also called Bhuvanagiri, crowns an isolated oval monolith about 47 km from Hyderabad on the road to Warangal. Tradition holds that the Western Chalukya king Tribhuvanamalla Vikramaditya VI built it, and the fort was named Tribhuvanagiri after him; the name later became Bhuvanagiri and then Bhongir. From the south the rock is said to look like a tortoise and from the west like a sleeping elephant. The fort is linked to the Kakatiya queen Rudramadevi and her grandson Prataparudra, and was later held for a long time by the Qutb Shahis. Its entrance recalls the Fateh Darwaza of Golconda, and inside are granaries, military quarters and courtyards. A Shiva temple with a black Nandi stands on the hill. The climb up the rock is a popular short outing from Hyderabad.

places.name: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam
places.summary: The great masonry dam on the Krishna, with Buddhist relics from Nandikonda in its museum.
places.seoTitle: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam: Krishna River Dam and Nandikonda Buddhist Relics
places.seoDescription: Nagarjuna Sagar on the Krishna in Nalgonda: the 124 m masonry dam behind Telangana's rice harvest, and the Buddhist relics of Nandikonda.

overview.text: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam spans the Krishna River in Nalgonda district. Built between 1955 and 1967, after Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated the work on 10 December 1955, the masonry dam straddles the border with Andhra Pradesh and is run jointly by the two states. Rising 124 metres and 1.6 km long, with 26 flood gates, it stores a vast reservoir whose waters irrigate the surrounding farmland, and Telangana Tourism credits it with the region's title of 'Rice Bowl of India'. Next to it lies Nandikonda, a small village on the river that was part of the Ikshvaku kingdom. Excavations here uncovered many ancient Buddhist structures, including pillared halls and monasteries, and the relics found in a series of digs are displayed in the museum at Nagarjuna Sagar.

overview.text: Medak is a district town in northern Telangana, originally known as Methukudurgam, a name linked to the fine rice grown in the area. It was part of the Kakatiya and Bahmani kingdoms, then of the Golconda Sultanate, the Mughal Empire and finally the Nizam's dominions, and coins of the Satavahana kings have been found at nearby Kondapur. Hindu, Christian, Muslim and Buddhist influences all show in its buildings. The town's hill fort, begun by the Kakatiyas and developed by the Qutb Shahis, stands about 90 metres above the plains with tiers of walls and bastions, and still holds a 10-foot Dutch-made brass gun. Medak Cathedral is one of its best-known sights. Nearby are a Qutb Shahi mosque at Komtoor, the Kuchadri Venkateswara temple, Pocharam Wildlife Sanctuary and the Edupayala temple.

places.name: Falaknuma Palace
places.summary: The Nizam's Italian-marble palace on a hill above the Old City, now a heritage hotel.
places.seoTitle: Falaknuma Palace, Hyderabad: The Nizam's Hilltop Palace
places.seoDescription: Falaknuma Palace, 5 km from Charminar: the Paigah and Nizam palace in Italian marble by William Ward Marret, restored and now a heritage hotel.

overview.text: Falaknuma Palace sits on a hillock about 5 km from Charminar, looking out over Hyderabad's Old City. Its name means 'like the sky' or 'mirror of the sky' in Urdu. Built for the Paigah nobles and later a favourite of the Nizam of Hyderabad, it was designed by the English architect William Ward Marret and finished in Italian marble, with stained-glass windows and a plan said to resemble a scorpion, with two wings extending to the north. Inside are frescoed and gilded ceilings in the State Reception Room, a library of English, Urdu and Persian books, Venetian chandeliers, a billiards room and a 2-ton manually operated organ in the ballroom. The palace stayed private to the Nizam's family for nearly a century; from 2000 about 1,000 artisans worked for nearly a decade to restore it, and today it is a heritage hotel.

places.name: Chowmahalla Palace
places.summary: The Nizams' palace of four courts beside Charminar, now a museum.
places.seoTitle: Chowmahalla Palace, Hyderabad: Seat of the Nizams
places.seoDescription: Chowmahalla Palace near Charminar: the Asaf Jahi seat of power, with four neoclassical palaces, the Khilwat durbar hall and the Nizams' vintage cars.

overview.text: Chowmahalla Palace, close to Charminar in Hyderabad's Old City, was the seat of the Asaf Jahi dynasty, which ruled from 1720 to 1948, and the official residence of the Nizams. Its name means 'four palaces'. Work on the present palace began in the 18th century, and the oldest part, the southern courtyard, has four neoclassical palaces facing one another across a garden and pond, with Ionic and Corinthian columns. The northern courtyard shows Mughal domes and Persian stucco work. Its heart is the Khilwat Mubarak, the pillared durbar hall with a marble platform for the royal seat and 19 Belgian-crystal chandeliers. The palace once covered 45 acres; 12 remain. The Nizam's family restored it and opened it as a museum in January 2005, with displays on the Nizams' lives and a collection of vintage cars including a Rolls-Royce.

places.name: Qutb Shahi Tombs
places.summary: The domed tombs of the Golconda kings, a kilometre from Golconda Fort.
places.seoTitle: Qutb Shahi Tombs, Hyderabad: Royal Tombs near Golconda
places.seoDescription: The Qutb Shahi Tombs near Golconda Fort, Hyderabad: granite domed tombs of the Golconda kings in the Ibrahim Bagh gardens.

overview.text: The Qutb Shahi Tombs lie about a kilometre north of Golconda Fort's Banjara Darwaza and hold the kings of the Golconda Sultanate, buried together in a single royal necropolis amid the landscaped Ibrahim Bagh gardens. Built by the Qutb Shahis themselves, they are among Hyderabad's oldest monuments and blend Persian, Pathan and Hindu styles in grey granite with stucco ornament. Each tomb is a domed building on a square base, ringed by pointed arches, and rises 9 to 15 metres above its terrace; smaller ones are single-storeyed, the larger ones two-storeyed, and the greatest reaches 42.5 metres. The domes were once covered in blue and green tiles, of which only a few pieces remain. Neglected after the dynasty fell, the tombs were restored under Salar Jung III, and today they are usually seen together with Golconda Fort.

places.summary: An ancient Svetambara Jain shrine on the Hyderabad–Warangal road.
places.seoTitle: Kolanupaka Jain Temple (Kulpakji), Telangana
places.seoDescription: Kolanupaka (Kulpakji) Jain temple, 77 km from Hyderabad: idols of Rishabha, Neminath and a jade Mahavira; a key Svetambara Jain pilgrimage.

overview.text: The Kolanupaka Jain temple, known to pilgrims as Kulpakji, stands in the village of Kolanupaka about 77 km from Hyderabad on the Hyderabad–Warangal highway. It is said to be more than two thousand years old, and in its present form more than eight hundred, and Kolanupaka was a prominent centre of Jainism in Telangana from early times. The main shrine houses three idols: Rishabha, the first Tirthankara, popularly called Adinath and known here as Manikya Deva; Neminath; and Mahavira, whose 130 cm statue is said to be carved from a single piece of jade. Eight idols of other Tirthankaras flank the main temple, with Simandar Swami and Mata Padmavati on either side. Kulpakji remains an important pilgrimage for the Svetambara Jains of South India.

places.name: Rajahmundry (Rajamahendravaram)
places.summary: Andhra's river city on the Godavari: ghats, bridges, temples and Papi Hills cruises.
places.seoTitle: Rajahmundry: Godavari Ghats, Papi Hills Cruise, Getting There
places.seoDescription: Rajahmundry on the Godavari: the rail bridges, ghats, Dowleswaram Barrage, Papi Hills boat cruises and nearby Pancharama temples; best October–February.

overview.text: Rajahmundry, officially Rajamahendravaram, stretches along the eastern bank of the Godavari and is one of Andhra Pradesh's oldest cities. Often called the cultural capital of the region and the birthplace of the Telugu language, it combines literary heritage with river life: morning rituals on the ghats, quiet boat rides and sunsets over the water. Its best-known landmark is the Godavari rail bridge, with views at sunrise and sunset. In the city are the ISKCON temple and the riverside Markandeya temple, and a short drive away is the Dowleswaram Barrage, where the Godavari divides into canals that water the delta. The most memorable trip is a boat cruise through the narrow, forested gorges of the Papi Hills. Temples around the city include Draksharamam, Bikkavolu and Kumararama at Samalkot.

best_time.text: October to February is the peak season, when the weather is cool for sightseeing, river cruises and festivals.

how_to_reach.text: Rajahmundry Airport, about 17 km from the city centre, has flights to Hyderabad, Chennai and Bangalore. The railway station is 5 km from the centre, with frequent trains from Hyderabad, Vijayawada, Chennai and Bengaluru. By road the city is on NH216, with regular buses from Hyderabad, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam.

places.name: Kurnool

places.seoTitle: Kurnool: Konda Reddy Fort, Belum Caves, Yaganti, Ahobilam
places.seoDescription: Kurnool, gateway of Rayalaseema: the Konda Reddy Fort, and a base for Belum Caves, Orvakal Rock Garden, Yaganti, Ahobilam and Rollapadu sanctuary.

overview.text: Kurnool is often called the 'Gateway of Rayalaseema'. In the city stands the Konda Reddy Fort, built under the Vijayanagara Empire, whose weathered ramparts carry ancient Persian and Arabic inscriptions and whose watch tower still looks over the city; a tunnel once ran from it under the river. Kurnool is mainly a base for the region's sights. Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary, 614 sq km of grassland, protects the endangered Great Indian Bustard and Lesser Florican. The Belum Caves are the subcontinent's second-largest cave system. Yaganti's temple has a single stone image of Shiva and Parvati, and Ahobilam worships all nine forms of Narasimha. Mahanandi, the Ketavaram rock paintings and the Orvakal Rock Garden, 20 km away, complete the circuit, and the local food is famously spicy.

how_to_reach.text: The nearest major airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad. Kurnool City railway station serves the city.

places.seoTitle: Orvakal (Oravakallu) Rock Garden near Kurnool
places.seoDescription: Orvakal Rock Garden, 20 km from Kurnool: strange igneous rock formations and pools for walks, rock climbing, camping and photography.

overview.text: Orvakal (Oravakallu) Rock Garden lies about 20 km from Kurnool in the rough country of southern Andhra Pradesh. It is a landscape of strange, weathered rock formations and boulders scattered among pools and greenery, with walkways cut through the rock that lead visitors past rock-cut sculptures and ancient cave temples. A local legend says Shiva threw stones from the surrounding hills to create the formations and keep demons away. The park is a favourite for photography and picnics, and it also suits more active visitors: there are trails for walking and hiking, rock-climbing spots and designated camping areas where you can spend a night under the stars. Birds and butterflies add to the scene. It makes an easy half-day trip from Kurnool, and it is open from 9 am to 6 pm.

places.summary: Sathya Sai Baba's town, built around the Prasanthi Nilayam ashram.

places.seoDescription: Puttaparthi, Andhra Pradesh: Sathya Sai Baba's Prasanthi Nilayam ashram, the Chaitanya Jyoti Museum and planetarium; best November–February.

overview.text: Puttaparthi is a small town in the plains of Anantapur district, believed to be the birthplace of the spiritual leader Sathya Sai Baba. Once called Gollapalli, the 'village of cowherds', it took its present name, meaning 'the township that sprang from anthills', from a local legend. The town grew around Prasanthi Nilayam, the 'abode of peace', Baba's ashram, which remains its spiritual heart with daily rituals and gatherings. Visitors enter through a gopuram archway and can see the Chaitanya Jyoti Museum on Baba's life, the Sri Sathya Sai Space Theatre planetarium, the Samadhi shrine where he rests, and the nearby Satyabhama temple, with the Chitravathi River flowing past. Penukonda fort, the temple of Lepakshi and the Jayamangali Blackbuck Reserve are all a short drive away.

how_to_reach.text: The nearest airport is Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru. Incredible India lists Anantapur as the nearest railway station.

overview.text: Maredumilli is a forest village in the East Godavari hills, about 85 km from Rajahmundry, that the Forest Department has developed for eco-tourism. Its semi-evergreen forests and rolling country are rich in wildlife, and the area is best known for its waterfalls: Jalatharangini, Amruthadhara and Rampa are the most popular, with Polluru waterfall about 65 km away. Visitors come to camp, go boating and birdwatching, and follow the many forest trails. The Manyam viewpoint looks over the hills, Bhupathupalem Reservoir is about 21 km from the village, and the Gudisa hill station is about 40 km away and often added to the same route. Food is part of the draw: bamboo chicken and bamboo biryani are traditional tribal dishes cooked inside bamboo stems.

how_to_reach.text: Rajahmundry has the nearest airport, with limited domestic flights, and the closest railway station. Maredumilli is on the Bhadrachalam–Rajahmundry highway, so cabs, buses and rental cars run from Rajahmundry, Bhadrachalam, Kakinada and Visakhapatnam.

places.summary: A 16th-century Vijayanagara temple of frescoes, a hanging pillar and a giant Nandi.
places.seoTitle: Lepakshi Temple: Hanging Pillar, Frescoes, Giant Nandi
places.seoDescription: Lepakshi's Veerabhadra Temple, Andhra Pradesh: 16th-century Vijayanagara frescoes, the hanging pillar, Sita's footprint and the great monolithic Nandi.

overview.text: The Veerabhadra Temple at Lepakshi, close to the Karnataka border, is one of the most spectacular Vijayanagara temples and a centrally protected monument. Built in the 16th century and dedicated to Veerabhadra, a fierce form of Shiva, it stands on Kumarasailam, a low hill said to resemble a tortoise. Nearly every surface is carved or painted. The ceilings of the Natya Mandapa, the dance pavilion, carry murals from the Mahabharata, Ramayana and Puranas, centred on a huge painting of Veerabhadra, and these are among the only surviving frescoes of the period. The famous hanging pillar seems to float above the floor, a footprint in the stone is believed to be Sita's, and a seven-hooded serpent shelters a Shiva linga. The Kalyana Mandapa was left unfinished. A short walk away, a monolithic Nandi 15 feet high and 27 feet long faces the temple.

places.seoDescription: Srisailam in the Nallamala Hills: the Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga temple, darshan timings, Akka Mahadevi caves, and the 9 pm–6 am forest road closure.

overview.text: Srisailam is a temple town in the Nallamala Hills of Andhra Pradesh, high above the Krishna River. Its Mallikarjuna temple, dedicated to Shiva as Mallikarjuna Swamy, is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas, and the town is also a Shakti peetha, and millions of pilgrims come each year. Legend links it to Shiva's cosmic dance to humble the demon Tarakasura and to the devotee Markandeya. The complex of carved shrines, mandapas and gopurams in the Dravidian style draws pilgrims all year, above all at Maha Shivaratri. Around the town are the Srisailam Dam on the Krishna, the Sakshi Ganapati temple, the Akka Mahadevi caves, Pathalaganga on the river and the Chenchu Lakshmi Tribal Museum. Srisailam is 231 km from Hyderabad, and the forest roads are closed at night.

places.summary: The 'King of Forts': 15 small forts on a rocky hill in Anantapur district.
places.seoTitle: Gooty Fort: The 'King of Forts' in Anantapur
places.seoDescription: Gooty Fort, Anantapur district: a shell-shaped hill fortress of 15 small forts, 108 wells and Morari Rao's chess pavilion; open 9–6, best November–February.

overview.text: Gooty Fort, or Ravadurg, crowns a group of steep rocky hills more than 680 metres high above the town of Gooty in Anantapur district. It is a centrally protected monument and an unusual design: a shell-shaped complex of 15 small forts, each with its own gateway, joined by an outer wall with bastions. An inscription of the Vijayanagara king Bukkaraya calls it the 'King of Forts'. Its present form was laid out by the Vijayanagara kings and later altered by the Marathas, the British and the Nizams. A paved path winds from the base to the summit, past a granary, a gunpowder magazine, rock-cut reservoirs and a remarkable 108 wells. At the top are temples, a dargah and a small clifftop pavilion where the Maratha general Morari Rao is said to have played chess, with wide views and fine sunsets.

places.summary: A Vijayanagara hill fort near Tirupati with the Raja Mahal museum.
places.seoTitle: Chandragiri Fort near Tirupati: Raja Mahal Museum
places.seoDescription: Chandragiri Fort near Tirupati: a 25-acre Vijayanagara hill fort with the three-storeyed Raja Mahal museum and Rani Mahal; open 10 am–5 pm.

overview.text: Chandragiri Fort stands on a rocky hill outside Tirupati, its 25 acres looking over green plains and rolling hills. Its name means 'hill of the moon', after a feature of its design. It was founded in the 11th century by Yadava rulers and strengthened by the Vijayanagara Empire in the 15th; the Gajapati king Kapilendra Dev took it in 1460, and the emperor Krishnadevaraya stayed here on his pilgrimages to Tirumala. The fort is divided into lower and upper parts. In the crescent-shaped lower fort stand the three-storeyed Raja Mahal, now a museum of weapons, sculptures, coins and documents, and the two-storeyed Rani Mahal, along with ruined temples and mandapas. The upper fort, reached by a demanding climb, has ramparts, watchtowers and wide views.

places.seoTitle: Talakona Waterfall near Tirupati: Treks and Forest
places.seoDescription: Talakona Waterfall near Tirupati: a 270-foot fall into an emerald pool in the Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve, with treks and rare wildlife; open sunrise–sunset.

overview.text: Talakona Waterfall lies in the forested Seshachalam hills of the Eastern Ghats in Tirupati district, a short drive from the temple town. Several mountain streams join to form the fall, which plunges about 270 feet through mist into a natural pool of emerald-green water at its base, where visitors cool off or sit quietly by the water. Local legend says the water has healing powers and that mythical Yakshas guard the falls. Talakona is part of the Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve, and its forests shelter rare and threatened species such as the Indian giant squirrel and the slender loris. Hiking routes lead to hidden caves, viewpoints and smaller waterfalls, and the area is popular for trekking, rock climbing, rappelling and birdwatching. The site is open from sunrise to sunset.

places.name: Kailasagiri
places.summary: Visakhapatnam's hilltop park, with a ropeway, sea views and a giant Shiva-Parvati statue.
places.seoTitle: Kailasagiri, Visakhapatnam: Ropeway, Shiva-Parvati Statue, Timings
places.seoDescription: Kailasagiri hill park in Visakhapatnam: ropeway, sea views, the 40-foot Shiva-Parvati statue and toy train; park open 10 am–8 pm.

overview.text: Kailasagiri is a hilltop park above Visakhapatnam, with wide views over the city and the sea. Created by the Visakhapatnam Urban Development Authority and named after Shiva, it was declared the 'Best Tourist Spot' by the Andhra Pradesh government in 2003. The hill is known for two landmark statues: a 40-foot figure of Shiva and Parvati, and a 20-foot Shanku Chakra Namam, the conch, discus and mark of Vishnu. Visitors can drive up, take one of two stairways, or ride the ropeway from the foot of the hill, which gives fine views on the way. At the top are gardens, a toy train, the ship-shaped Titanic viewpoint, play areas and amusement rides, and an annual floral festival fills the gardens with colour, making it one of the city's favourite family outings.

items.body: Shiva-Parvati statue; Titanic viewpoint; toy train

places.name: Kanipakam Vinayaka Temple
places.summary: Ganesha temple near Chittoor where the self-manifested idol sits in a well.
places.seoTitle: Kanipakam Vinayaka Temple: History, Brahmotsavam, Getting There
places.seoDescription: Kanipakam Vinayaka Temple, Chittoor: a Chola-built shrine whose self-manifested Ganesha sits in a water-filled well; 21-day Brahmotsavam from Vinayaka Chavithi.

overview.text: The Sri Varasidhi Vinayaka Swamy temple at Kanipakam, in Chittoor district, is one of the most revered Ganesha temples in South India. Its idol is believed to be self-manifested. Legend tells of three brothers, one mute, one deaf and one blind, who struck a hard object while digging a well and were healed; the villagers found an image of Ganesha seated in the water, and its base has never been found. The idol still sits in the water-filled well, with only the knees and belly visible, and devotees believe it grows: a silver armour made about 50 years ago no longer fits. The temple was built in the early 11th century by Kulottunga Chola I and enlarged in 1336 under the Vijayanagara emperors. Its 21-day Brahmotsavams, beginning on Vinayaka Chavithi, are the best time to see it.

items.body: Chittoor station and bus stand about 11–12 km; Tirupati airport about 85–90 km

places.name: Gandikota Fort and Gorge
places.summary: A ruined hill fort above the red gorge of the Penna River in Kadapa district.
places.seoTitle: Gandikota: Penna River Gorge, Fort, Camping, Getting There
places.seoDescription: Gandikota, Kadapa district: an ASI-protected fort above the Penna River gorge, with temples, a mosque, canyon treks and riverside camping.

overview.text: Gandikota is a village and ruined fort on the right bank of the Penna River, 15 km from Jammalamadugu in Kadapa district. Its name comes from the gorge (gandi) that the river has cut between the Erramala hills, narrowing it to about 100 metres between cliffs of quartzite. A sand fort was first made here in 1123; the site grew into a major stronghold under the Pemmasani Nayakas and later passed to the Golconda Sultanate, which added Islamic buildings. Today it is an ASI-protected monument. Inside the walls are the ruined Madhava and Ranganatha temples, the Jamia Masjid with two minarets, a large vaulted granary, a pigeon tower and an old cannon. Visitors camp outside the fort and on the riverbank, and a downhill trek leads through the canyon to the water.

items.title: Getting there
items.body: Muddanuru station 26 km; buses from Jammalamadugu

items.title: Activities
items.body: Fort walk, canyon trek, riverside camping

places.name: Belum Caves
places.summary: India's second-largest cave network, with stalactites and an underground stream.
places.seoTitle: Belum Caves, Andhra Pradesh: India's Second-Largest Cave System
places.seoDescription: Belum Caves in Nandyal district: a 3.23 km limestone cave system with stalactites, stalagmites and the Pataalaganga stream; used by monks, open since 2002.

overview.text: The Belum Caves, near Belum village in Nandyal district, form a limestone cave system that extends for 3.23 km, the second-largest cave network in India. They were formed by water erosion and are full of karst features: stalactites, stalagmites and other formations, with spacious chambers between narrow passages, and sediments left by the Chitravathi River that once flowed through them. People used the caves as early as 4500 BCE, and Buddhist and Jain ascetics later meditated in their halls. Though long known to local people, they were first documented by the geologist Robert Bruce Foote in 1884 and mapped by a German team in the early 1980s. Protected since 1988, the caves opened to visitors in 2002. Pathways lead down to the deepest point, Pataalaganga, where an underground stream flows all year.

items.title: Don't miss
items.body: Pataalaganga, the underground stream at the deepest point

places.name: Kondapalli Fort
places.summary: A 14th-century hill fort by the Krishna, above the village of Kondapalli toys.
places.seoTitle: Kondapalli Fort near Vijayawada: History, Timings, Toys
places.seoDescription: Kondapalli Fort by the Krishna, NTR district: a 14th-century hill fort with a monolithic granite gate and Tanisha Mahal; village famous for wooden toys.

overview.text: Kondapalli Fort, also called Kondapalli Kota, stands on a hill beside the Krishna River west of Kondapalli village in NTR district. Dating from the 14th century, it was first a place of leisure and trade, and it passed from the Reddy kingdom to the Qutb Shahis, the Mughals and finally the British, who turned it into a military training base. Winding paths through greenery lead up to stone-and-mortar walls that still stand tall. The entrance, the Dargah Darwaja, is carved from a single colossal granite boulder; inside are the remains of the royal court, the Tanisha Mahal, the Golconda Darwaza and the dargah of Gareeb Saheb, with fine views over the river. At the foot of the hill, Kondapalli village is famous for brightly painted wooden toys, handcrafted from the local ponuku wood.

items.title: Don't miss
items.body: Dargah Darwaja; Tanisha Mahal; Kondapalli toys in the village
